extracted.intended_audience: Incident Management Team members, Incident Commanders, and Public Information Officers involved in ICS/all-hazards incident transitions and deployments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for Incident Management Teams (IMTs) on transitioning into an ongoing incident, establishing operations during the first operational period, communications, documentation, and unified command interactions. Emphasizes professional conduct, information transfer, and practical checklists for team roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely posting of documentation when reproduction unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If time or machines don’t allow timely reproduction to meet demand, posting copies of it allows anyone interested enough to review it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unable to reproduce documents for distribution, post copies so stakeholders can review; this ensures access to plans and reduces questions after the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and meaningful interaction with the responsible jurisdiction/agency
rubrics_metrics.description: When invited, an Incident Management Team is a guest expected to perform a mission; transfer information to the responsible jurisdiction throughout the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop rapport with the responsible jurisdiction contact, act as an extension of that jurisdiction, and focus on pleasing that person(s) by keeping them informed and involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly and complete paperwork
rubrics_metrics.description: Time records, documentation package, fiscal records, a team’s Narrative Report and related documentation must be orderly and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document actions thoroughly — historical records are permanent; poor documentation can overshadow good operational performance. Include internal audits and cost apportionment where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visual presentations for information sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the current Incident Action Plan, next operational period, news, meeting schedules, directions to drop points, Medical Plan, Safety Message, parking directions, menu of the day, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals let people self-serve information; assume people can read. Use visuals to reduce repetitive briefings and keep personnel informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitioning definition and goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition: 'a process to familiarize a group of persons to a situation in progress as well as setting agency strategic priorities for its control.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide real-time knowledge and local operating procedures so the IMT can assume mission; the transition should transfer the most information possible and be documented for later reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the transfer during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of the transition is required for later reference; these documents become the cornerstone to an IMT’s actions and incident history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completed transition forms, Delegation of Authority, and other documents are collected and stored as part of the historical record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Agency Administrator Briefing / transition form
rubrics_metrics.description: An Agency Administrator Briefing to IMT form provides a good basis to transfer items proven necessary on past deployments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call the responsible agency before activation to learn if they use a transition form; if not, suggest one and fax it. Expect forms to be incomplete; jointly filling the form may be necessary. Review form content yearly for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal transition timing, location, and required attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal transition takes place at a specified time and location with the completed form; a vast majority of team members need to be present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiate realistic timing (IC may need to) to allow key personnel to arrive. Be aware some agencies expect command to be assumed immediately by first arrival—manage expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set a professional tone for the briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: The team should set a professional tone for the briefing by being punctual, identifiable, prepared and attentive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuality, clear identification, preparation, and attentiveness influence perceptions and aid information transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform and identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All team members should be in well-marked PPE or agency work uniform with issued team identification clearly displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear identification reduces confusion, establishes professionalism, and helps jurisdictional partners recognize team roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team formation and materials during briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members should form a group close to the agency speaker with notepaper and, hopefully, a copy of the completed transition form available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a completed form is not available, use a blank form to guide questions; determine roles of other attendees and who they represent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductions of key personnel and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency administrator briefing should start with introductions of key agency personnel by name, title and incident function; teams should introduce themselves by name and position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear identification of people and roles helps later coordination and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency administrator briefing content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency administrator typically provides an overview of the incident’s history, projections, resource status and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to assist the briefing; this overview frames the IMT’s strategic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiate and facilitate a question period
rubrics_metrics.description: After the agency administrator briefing, the IC should negotiate a question period for team members to retrieve necessary information that might not have been dispensed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate by function (e.g., 'resource unit leader, any further questions?') and keep questions restricted to pertinent issues only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the team start time
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the briefing, the agency administrator and IC should have set an actual time for team actions to begin on the incident; this should be part of the briefing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not mentioned, raise it during the briefing; documentary clarity on start time avoids confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect any written materials or displays presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect any written materials or displays presented to the team by the agency administrator, regardless of their value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even seemingly low-value materials may contain important details; gather everything for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: IAIC briefing needs and information sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Initial Attack Incident Commander will brief the team; the team will need the best incident information available (what has happened, what has been attempted, projections, resource status, locations, and serviceability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain situation maps, weather forecasts, traffic maps, and ICS Form 201 if available. Recognize IAIC may be trusted and useful, but also may be discouraged or negative—evaluate information accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction on future involvement of agency personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: The team will need direction on future involvement of agency personnel currently on the incident (stay and incorporate or release and when).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This decision is between the agency administrator and IAIC; get clarity to plan staffing and incorporation of local personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request local liaison assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams can leave a lasting positive impression if a request is made to have a 'local' person assigned to them for local knowledge availability; routinely request IAIC to stay assigned and available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A local person provides continuity and area knowledge; ask for their continued availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of received information across team
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members must assemble as a unit to affirm dispensed information and conduct a strategy meeting; confirm that all team members have the same information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group confirmation avoids disjointed knowledge. Identify and resolve information differences before acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set general strategy and specific objectives for the first operational period
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on known status, a general strategy must be set; IC can list objectives/goals for non-operations functions (ICS Form 202).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize actions (e.g., logistics develop a 2,000 person camp); post visual displays of priorities to communicate expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Delegation of Authority / Delineation of Roles and Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed copy of the Delineation of Roles and Authorities – Administrator’s Instructions (Delegation of Authority) should be given to the IMT along with the Agency Administrator Briefing form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents clearly set team actions into motion and are critical for non-agency incidents or partial assignments; obtain explicit, signed authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify specific roles/authorities for partial or single-function assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a team activation is for an assignment other than assuming command, very specific roles and authorities must be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a team deployed to manage care and housing of evacuees only must have their specific role and authority defined and understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist jurisdiction with transition paperwork and process
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the best leadership moves is to 'walk' the jurisdiction through the Transition Briefing (w/form) and assist with the Delegation of Authority completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ensure full understanding and reduces future misunderstandings; time invested early pays off during deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify inclusion of all key jurisdiction personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if all of the jurisdiction’s key personnel are involved in delegation to a team (e.g., county sheriff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count the noses; missing key stakeholders can cause major issues later—ensure all appropriate officials know and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be thorough during the first transition opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: This may be the first, last, and only opportunity to gather information before the team assumes an incident; go slow and be thorough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try not to let key players leave before questions are answered; capture as much information as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect shortages of information during the first operational period
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and expect shortages of information (ordered resource ETAs, situation reports, maps, timely reports of injuries/costs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop adaptations to work around missing info; set expectations and plan contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-assign functional tasks to gather info prior to arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct functional roles to gather best available information prior to arriving to shortstop 'it’s lost in the system' syndrome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: logistics person to dispatch to get agency documents and ordering procedures; planning person to retrieve incident documentation, news releases, cost calculations, weather, and past incidents; operations person to recon the current situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multiple briefings for late resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multiple briefings for 'late' resources; operations may send a representative to briefing while another recons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on review of current strategies and resources by operations greatly enhances IAP development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-extension and recognize burnout
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members routinely work extended hours; studies show burnout occurs at about hour 11 when under stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor personnel for diminishing returns on efficiency, production, and safety; avoid overwork that can lead to mistakes or unsafe situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff key positions with a second person / rotate for rest
rubrics_metrics.description: Team positions having a second person assigned should consciously divide workload and allow rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs should monitor divisions of workload; the non-active partner should rest to relieve their partner when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 24-hour operational periods to ease workload compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of twenty-four hour operational periods has proven to ease compression of time for some functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer operational periods provide more calendar time to accomplish tasks, though overall workload remains; consider when advantageous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require deputy positions when extended operations expected
rubrics_metrics.description: Team guidelines can require certain sections to have deputy positions filled whenever the crunch is expected to exceed a certain operational period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate staffing shortfalls and fill deputies proactively to maintain function continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare contingency plans when additional staffing is unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience teaches to expect the unexpected and that ordering more assistance is not always an answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have alternative plans available when additional staff, travel, or availability prevent augmenting personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overestimating production during start-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams commonly overestimate what can be produced in the first operational period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realistically assess whether an IAP, next IAP, contingency planning, facilities development, communications organization, and drop point marking can all be achieved; set realistic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize tasks at the function-head level and share impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual function heads must prioritize specific work; if priorities impact other functions, share this with the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full team meeting 4–5 hours into the first operational period helps share projected shortfalls and accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be adaptive and creative while avoiding low-yield schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize when the impossible just takes longer; be adaptive and creative but guard against expending time on schemes with marginal success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use past experience and the collective knowledge of the team to find workable solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage cross-training and open idea sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to recognize abilities of other team members; allow cross-trained staff to assist where workload is light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage brainstorming at meetings, prioritize needs, and have members assist across functions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications categories: intra-team, intra-incident, external
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications during deployment break down into three categories: intra-team, intra-incident, and external; failure in any will impact team success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for all three categories explicitly; use appropriate tools and protocols for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster intra-team communication and inclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sincerely welcome new members; actively maintain an atmosphere that advocates smooth and healthy communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address obstacles such as agency affiliation hesitancy, rank-related reluctance, or perceived ability gaps; ICs and section chiefs should cultivate openness and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team guidelines should prescribe meeting processes and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Team guidelines can describe and structure meetings (expectations on length, contents, attendees, documentation) and require member participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List expected meetings (Transition Briefing, Strategy Meeting, Planning Meetings, Operational Briefings, Daily Team Meetings, Demobilization Planning, Transition Out Briefing, Post Incident Team Critique) and define roles like scribe or meeting facilitator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document meetings and decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams should develop a standard procedure for documenting all meetings; many key decisions will require later review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign a scribe or delegate documentation duties in team guidelines; post agendas with outcome expectations and required attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep incident troops informed with accessible displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep troops informed via routinely updated bulletin boards, single page briefings, and visual displays within the ICP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design communication so personnel can find needed information without asking managers; frees manager time and reduces confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a library of pre-developed standard documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each team should have pre-developed 'standard' documents (motel policies, personnel standards, release priorities, etc.) available from personal word processors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of standard templates speeds response and ensures consistency; build and update upon each activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IAP legibility and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An IAP that cannot be read is less than worthless; it must be reproducible and clean for distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use InciNet or other computer systems if available; have laptop copies of programs or legible handwriting; use GIS-generated maps in 8.5x11 format for reproducible maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include communications information on assignment lists and communication plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assure all pertinent information is on each Assignment List (ICS Form 204) and the Communication Plan (ICS Form 217); include LCES on Assignment Lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment Lists reflect communications specific to resource assignments; build flexibility while keeping troops informed when personnel are reassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include staff cell phone numbers and maintain a directory
rubrics_metrics.description: Each IAP should include a listing of staff cell phone numbers; begin building a cell phone/pager directory early and update with every new IAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In areas with adequate cell coverage, free radio traffic for operations by using cell phones for non-operational messaging; maintain and update directories on portable word processors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use radio for operations and be cautious with cell phone use
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain communications should NOT be conducted via cell phone; use radios for operations messages so others can eavesdrop and remain informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolating communications via private phone calls can leave others unaware; choose communication medium by intended audience and operational necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain radio discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations leaders and incident dispatchers need to maintain radio discipline to eliminate untimely use of congested airwaves and maintain a professional-sounding incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train and enforce radio discipline to preserve channel availability for urgent operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: External communications: ICS Form 209 completeness, accuracy, timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The most off-incident reviewed document is the Incident Status Summary (ICS Form 209). Completeness, accuracy and timeliness are paramount; there are deadlines that must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Form 209s as critical for resource allocation and off-incident decision-making; submit on time and confirm receipt/timetable with receivers early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconfirm required off-incident document timetables and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many documents required to be transmitted off an incident; reconfirm early during the incident the timetable and method for each with the receiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wasted time chasing late or incomplete documents by clarifying expectations and methods early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency administrator briefings should be forthright and pre-checked
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency administrator briefing times/methods are set during Transition Briefing; reviewing the latest intelligence just prior will allow transmission of the best information while making a professional presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being forthright and honest helps off-incident decision makers; update briefing material just before presentation for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore local internet provider assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some local Internet providers have been known to provide access for incident use free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check logistics options early to determine if free incident internet access is available and how to access it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify legitimacy of Unified Command and agency responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When transitioning into a Unified Command incident, determine if it is legitimately Unified Command — i.e., 'allow all agencies with responsibility for the incident, either geographical or functional, to manage an incident.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear, ask the agency administrator for clarification; beware of nominal inclusions that do not confer actual jurisdiction or responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and communicate a single ordering point under Unified Command
rubrics_metrics.description: Has a single ordering point been established? Agencies must agree on a single point for ordering additional resources/supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incident Commanders must agree on the method, advise their agencies, and ensure all agency personnel know to process orders through the single point to avoid conflicting orders and resource allocation problems.
